summary: Louis H. Gray worked in linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Princeton University (~1892–1896) and Columbia University (~1896–1900), holding posts at Princeton (~1900–1902) and the University of Nebraska–Lincoln (~1921–1926).

Louis Havet was a scholar in linguistics and other fields. He studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1868–1872) under Michel Bréal and Abel Bergaigne, and later held a post at the Collège de France (1885–1925).

Louis Komjathy specializes in religious studies and sinology. He earned his PhD at Boston University (~2000–2005) and studied under Paul Rouzer. In ~2009, he became an assistant professor at the University of San Diego.
Louis Ligeti worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, sinology, and Tibetology. He studied at Eötvös Loránd University (~1921–1925) and at the University of Paris (1925–1928) under Paul Pelliot.

Louis Renou was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Lycée Janson-de-Sailly, École nationale des langues orientales vivantes, and Faculty of Arts of Paris under Antoine Meillet. He held posts at the University of Paris (~1937–1947) and Institut de France (~1946–1966).

Louis de La Vallée Poussin specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Liège and under Charles de Harlez, Philippe Colinet, Sylvain Lévi, Victor Henry, and Hendrik Kern. He held professorships at Ghent University and the Free University of Brussels.

Louis-Mathieu Langlès worked in sinology, linguistics, and Indology. He studied under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy. He held posts at the Bibliothèque nationale de France (~1795–1824) and the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales (1796–1824).

Louise Child specializes in religious studies and Tibetology. She earned her PhD at the University of Leeds (~-2002), studying under Linda Hogan and Ringu Tulku, and later held a teaching post at the University of Leeds.

Loukram Ibempishak Devi focuses on philosophy and Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD at Gauhati University in 1999 under doctoral supervisor Sibnath Sarma, having also studied under S. Shyamkishore Singh and S. Lokendrajit Singh.
Luboš Bělka works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. He studied at Masaryk University from ~1978 to 1983 and held a post there in ~1993.

Luca Maria Olivieri works in history, archaeology, and Indology. He completed his doctoral degree at the Free University of Berlin (~2006–2010) and held posts at the Istituto Italiano per il Medio ed Estremo Oriente (~2011) and Ca' Foscari University of Venice (2020–2021).
Lucia Galli specializes in Tibetology. She completed her doctorate at the University of Oxford (~2010–2015) under the supervision of Ulrike Roesler and later held a post at the University of Oxford.
Lucian Scherman worked in Indology and other fields. He studied at the Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich from ~1883 to 1887 and later held a post there from ~1893 to 1936.

Luciano Petech worked in Tibetology, history, and archaeology. He studied under Giuseppe Tucci (~1932–1936). He held posts at the University of Allahabad (1938–1946), University of Naples "L'Orientale" (1947), Sapienza University of Rome (1955–1984), and Istituto Italiano per il Medio ed Estremo Oriente.

Lucy Annette Jones focuses on Tibetology and religious studies. She earned her PhD at Rice University (~2005–2011) under Anne Carolyn Klein and Edith Wyschogrod, and studied with Lopon Tenzin Namdak and Tenzin Wangyal Rinpoche.

Ludo Rocher was an Indologist who earned his degrees at Ghent University (~1944–1950). He held posts at the Free University of Brussels (~1951–1966), Deccan College (1953–1955), and the University of Pennsylvania (~1966–2002).

Ludwig Alsdorf was an Indologist who studied at Ludwigsgymnasium Saarbrücken, the University of Hamburg under Walther Schubring, and Humboldt University of Berlin under Heinrich Lüders. He held a chair at the University of Hamburg beginning in 1950.
Ludwig Heller was an Indologist. He studied at the University of Göttingen from ~1889 to 1894 and later held a post at the University of Greifswald from ~1897 to 1934.

Ludwig Lange worked in linguistics, history, and archaeology. He studied at the University of Göttingen under Theodor Benfey and at Leipzig University. He held posts at Göttingen, Charles University, the University of Giessen, and Leipzig University.

Ludwig Wittgenstein was a philosopher who studied at Bundesrealgymnasium Linz Fadingerstraße, Technische Hochschule Berlin, University of Manchester, and Trinity College, Cambridge. He held academic posts at Trinity College, Cambridge (1929–1947) and the University of Cambridge (1939–1947).
